newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: QLD POLICE HAPPY WITH FANTASY INVESTIGATION
Queensland's Police Commissioner, Jim O'Sullivan, says police are close to finding the suppliers of the designer drug, Fantasy, which recently sent 10 people into comas on the Gold Coast.
Mr O'Sullivan, the Police Minister, Russell Cooper and other senior police spent yesterday discussing local policing issues with Gold Coast business representatives.
After the talks, the Commissioner said police were happy with the way their investigation was going.
MAN CHARGED WITH CAIRNS' FIRE ATTACK ON BOY MOVED
The man charged with the attempted unlawful killing of a six year old boy in a Cairns schoolyard is being transferred to a Brisbane jail for his own protection.
Corrective Services says 26-year-old Paul Wayne Streeton, of Adelaide, is being moved from Townsville to Moreton Prison today.
The accused has been kept under protection and constant observation in Townsville jail since the incident.
About half the inmates in Townsville are indigenous.
Tjandamurra O'Shane remains in the intensive care unit at the Royal Children's Hospital he's expected to undergo his second skin graft operation tomorrow.
FARMERS CALL FOR END TO RURAL DOCTOR SHORTAGES
The New South Wales Farmers Association wants the federal government to make policy adjustments to alleviate the acute shortage of rural doctors in Australia.
Association President Ian Donges says farmers have been pushing for several years to overcome the shortfall of up to 150 doctors in New South Wales.
He says some country centres are battling to get one doctor to practise there, when 20 years ago they had several.

Mr Donges says state and federal governments must combine to encourage doctors to rural areas, allocate Medicare provider numbers to regional doctors and require overseas doctors migrating to Australia to work initially in regional areas.
MAN DIES IN NSW MINING ACCIDENT
In New South Wales, a man has died in a mining accident in Lightning Ridge in the state's north-west.
Police say a sandstone roof in an opal mine collapsed while two men where working there yesterday afternoon.
Their wives alerted authorities when they failed to return home at the end of the day.
Police and Emergency Services found a 46 year old Lightning Ridge man alive in the rubble after midnight last night - he's in Lightning Ridge Hospital in a serious but stable condition.
The body of his companion, a 32 year old Walgett man, was removed a short time later.
Mining authorities are investigating the accident.
STEELWORKS MUST BE COMPETITIVE, BHP SAYS
BHP says any reinvestment in steelmaking at Newcastle, will be designed to make the operation internationally competitive.
BHP's Newcastle manager, Ron McNeilly, has told state Premier Bob Carr and steel unions that it may be the middle of next year before the company decides on the future of steel-making in the city.
But he promised to keep them informed.
Mr Carr says BHP has a strong social obligation to reinvest in steelmaking in Newcastle, but Mr McNeilly says any investment has to be financially responsible.
Steel unions are now seeking a meeting with the Federal government to ensure BHP renews steelmaking equipment nearing the end of its lifetime.
